home.checkFailed: Could not check. Is the server running?
home.contextEmptyText: Nothing would be injected for this project. Capture some memories first.

home.exampleRule1: Always run the tests before saying a task is done.
home.exampleRule2: Ask me before deleting files or changing the database.
home.exampleRule3: Keep answers short and show the commands I need to run.

home.introListens: While you work in Claude Code, Command Code or Codex, Aletheia quietly writes down what happened: what you decided, what you fixed, what to remember.
home.introRemembers: Everything stays on this computer. Secrets such as keys and passwords are removed before anything is saved.
home.introReminds: The next time you start a session, the tool gets a short summary of what you already decided, plus your rules. You stop repeating yourself.
home.knowsExample: “Retargeting only works for Meta campaigns” or “The deploy script needs Node 20.19.6”.
home.knowsSubtitle: Newest first. Aletheia writes these down by itself from your sessions.
home.loadFailed: Some information could not be loaded. Is the server running? Try: systemctl --user status aletheia.service

home.noteHint: It is saved as a pinned note and is shown at the start of every new session in this project.

home.ruleOff: Rule is off. It is kept; turn it on again any time.

memory.heading: Knowledge
memory.hiddenFactsText: A fact you hide shows up here, and you can restore it.
memory.lede: Everything Aletheia has remembered, in one place that all your tools read. Search it, add a note, or hide what is wrong.

memory.noMemoriesText: Memories appear when a connected tool captures a session, or when you write one yourself.
memory.noResultsText: Nothing matched these words and filters.
memory.noteEmpty: Write a title or some text first.
memory.noteTextPlaceholder: What should every tool remember? Markdown works.

review.dupesEmptyText: Aletheia compares memories in your most recent project. Pairs that read almost the same show up here, so you can merge them or keep both.
review.dupesHint: Memories that read almost the same. Keep both, or merge the newer into the older one.
review.idInvalid: An id is a whole number, for example 42.
review.keptApartDone: Kept apart. They will not be suggested again.
review.mergeIntoMessage: Row #{id} will be marked merged into #{target}, and #{target} is kept. This cannot be undone from this page.
review.mergePairMessage: The older row #{a} is kept and #{b} is marked merged. This cannot be undone from this page.
review.mergePromptLabel: The id of the row to keep. This row is merged into it.
review.queueEmptyText: When two facts disagree, or a name could mean two things, the item lands here. You decide; nothing changes without you.
review.queueHint: Decide each item. Accept or reject can be undone for 8 seconds, and any decision can be reopened later.
review.rejected: Rejected. It moved to Resolved below.
rules.added2: Rule added. Write the files to put it in your tools.
rules.approved: Rule added. It is on, for every tool you write files for.
rules.confirmed: Rule confirmed. It is unchanged; only its last-confirmed date moved.
rules.doInstead: What the tool should do instead
rules.editedAdded: Edited and added. It is on, for every tool you write files for.
rules.emptyText: A rule is something you want every AI tool to follow. Write it once here, then write it into each tool's instruction file. You can also import the rules your tools already have.
rules.factHidden: Fact hidden from search and context. Nothing was deleted.
rules.importIntro: Reads the bullet lines from a tool's current instruction file and adds them as rules. Nothing is overwritten, and rules you already have are skipped.
rules.itemRestored: Restored. It is back in search and context.
rules.memoryHidden: Hidden from search and context. Nothing was deleted.
rules.minChars: The rule needs at least 6 characters.
rules.nameScope: Name the project or situation, or choose Everywhere.
rules.noDismissedText: Suggestions you dismiss are kept here, so you can restore them.
rules.noMatchText: Clear the filter to see every rule.
rules.noQuotes: No dated quotes were stored for this suggestion.
rules.noRun: No learning run has been recorded yet. Run it to scan your prompts for repeated corrections.
rules.noSourceEpisode: No source episode is linked to this fact.
rules.noSuggestionText: When you correct a tool the same way a few times, Aletheia suggests a rule here. Nothing is applied until you Approve it.
rules.onlyForTools: Only for these tools (none ticked means all tools)
rules.outOfSync.one: {count} tool out of sync with these rules. Open Write to tools to preview the difference.
rules.outOfSync.other: {count} tools out of sync with these rules. Open Write to tools to preview the difference.
rules.pinnedToast: Pinned. It stays at the top.
rules.rejected: Rejected. It is under Dismissed if you change your mind.

rules.replacedToast: Replaced with rule {id}. The old rule is kept.
rules.retired: Rule retired. It is turned off and kept, not deleted.

rules.runRecorded: Learning run recorded: found {found}, proposed {proposed}, errors {errors}.
rules.savedWriteAgain: Saved. Write the files again to update your tools.

rules.staleLine.one: {count} rule to re-check. Flagged rules stay on and keep syncing until you retire them.
rules.staleLine.other: {count} rules to re-check. Flagged rules stay on and keep syncing until you retire them.

rules.title: Title
rules.turnedOff: Rule turned off. It is kept, not deleted.
rules.turnedOn: Rule turned on. Write the files again to update your tools.
rules.typePath: Type the absolute path of the project folder.

rules.writeConfirm.other: This writes a managed block into the rules file of {count} tools ({tools}). A backup of each existing file is kept, and nothing outside the block changes. You can run Preview first to see the new content.

search.noMatch: No match. Try fewer or different words.

status.fixHint: To fix or change this, run:

team.alertsIntro: Rules match device, token, quota, sync, extraction and queue events. Webhook bodies are signed with HMAC-SHA256; private targets need explicit permission.
team.allowPrivate: Allow a private or local address
team.decisionHint: A decision stays on the board and in the brief.
team.leaveMessage: Your shared entries are withdrawn from the team, your project shares are removed and your sync token is revoked. This cannot be undone; an owner has to add you again.
team.noDeliveriesText: When a rule fires, each attempt is listed here, newest first.
team.noMatchText: Nothing this team shares matches those words.
team.noRulesText: A rule watches one event, such as a revoked token or a failed extraction, and writes a line to a file or posts to a webhook. Nothing is sent until you add one.
team.noTeamText: A team shares chosen projects with other people: a board of pins and decisions, a brief and search limited to what each member may see. Create one to start.
team.nothingPinnedText: Pinned memories and decisions of this project show up here.
team.pickProject: Share and pick a project first.
team.pinHint: Everyone who shares this project sees the note on the board.
team.placeHint: Webhook bodies are signed with HMAC-SHA256 when you set a secret. Private addresses need the box below.
team.projectsHint: Only these shared projects are visible to the member.
team.removeRuleMessage: It stops sending at once. Deliveries already in the feed stay. This cannot be undone; add the rule again if you need it.
team.revokeMessage: The member loses access at once and their sync token stops working on every device. Rows they shared stay with the team. This cannot be undone; add them again to restore access.
team.roleHint: A viewer reads, an editor also writes, an owner also manages members.
team.rulesError: Could not read the alert rules
team.sayWhere: Say where the alert goes: a file path or a webhook address.
team.teamIntro: Shared projects, a board of pins and decisions, a rule-based brief and search limited by each member's access. A viewer can read but not write.
team.tokenText: This token is shown once. Copy it now and hand it to the member; it cannot be read again.
team.viewerReadOnly: A viewer can read but not write.
tools.dataIntro: Two irreversible tools live here. Each one shows what it would do before it does it.
tools.e2eeOff: End-to-end encryption is off. Turn it on from the command line: aletheia sync enable-e2ee.
tools.eraseChoose: Choose a project, some ids or a date to erase.
tools.eraseIntro: Remove rows for good: by project, by id, or older than a date. Preview the report first. Erasing is locked until a preview found rows, then asks you to type ERASE.
tools.eraseProof: A pre-erase export is written first and a signed receipt after, so you keep proof of what was removed.
tools.eraseWarn: This deletes the matching memories, observations, episodes and facts, their search index and vectors, and the matching rows on paired devices. It cannot be undone.
tools.errLinks: Could not read the access links
tools.errStatus: Could not read the tool status
tools.hooksTip: Small scripts the tool runs so Aletheia can capture your sessions. The numbers are installed over expected.
tools.keepReceipt: Keep the receipt file. It proves what was removed; verify it below at any time.
tools.linksIntro: Read-only MCP links for remote clients such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop. The token travels in the Authorization header, never in the URL.
tools.mergeIntro: Fold a duplicate or worktree project into the main one. Preview the plan first: it lists how many rows move and how many duplicates are dropped, per table. Merging then asks you to type the source project’s name.
tools.mergeWarn: Every row of {source} moves to {target}, and rows {target} already has are dropped. This cannot be undone and {source} stops existing as a project. One audit entry records the counts.
tools.noActivityText: Every change made from this page, the command line or a tool is listed here, newest first.
tools.noDevicesText: Pair a second computer to keep one memory on both. Press Show pairing code, then run the join command on the other machine.
tools.noHooksFile: this tool has no hooks file
tools.noLinksText: Create a link to let one remote tool read your memory. Nothing is reachable from outside until you do.
tools.noMatchText: Try fewer filters or a wider date range.
tools.noRowsInTables: Neither project has rows in a project table.
tools.notJson: That text is not valid JSON.
tools.pairingHelp: Run this on the other machine. The code works once.
tools.pendingTip: Changes this device has not received yet.
tools.readOnlyStatus: Read-only status from {command}. Install, uninstall and connect stay on the command line; copy the commands below.
tools.receiptGenuine: The receipt is genuine: its signature matches.
tools.reportNote: Nothing was deleted. This is the report. Erasing writes a pre-erase export first, then a signed receipt.
tools.revokeDeviceMessage: Its token stops working on the next call, so it can no longer push or pull. The device keeps its own local copy. To use it again you pair it again.
tools.revokeLinkMessage: Any client using this token loses access at once. This cannot be undone; create a new link if you need one again.
tools.spoolTip: Events waiting on disk while the server is not reachable. They are sent when it is back.
tools.tokenOnce: The token is shown once. Copy it now; it cannot be shown again.
tools.typeSource: Type the source project name to confirm
tools.verifyIntro: Checks the signature of an erasure receipt against the local key.
